To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. A model of cell cycle progression in budding yeast based on the titration of Cdc28 against the number of SBF binding sites in the genome can recapitulate the observed size homeostasis in wild type cells and size phenotypes of mutants that alter ploidy and WHi5 copy number.

a model based on inhibitor dilution can explain the size of the wild type strain and mutants that alter the copy number of the WHI5 gene, whereas a model based on titration of Cdk activity against a constant number binding sites can explain the size homeostasis of the wild type, as well as the size of mutants with altered ploidy.

(1) inhibitor dilution can facilitate size homeo-stasis; (2) size homeostasis can be achieved by coupling cell growth to cell-cycle progression; (3) inhibitor dilution cannot explain the cell sizes of mutants that alter ploidy; (4) titration of CIn3 against a constant pool of SBF binding sites can explain size homeostasis, the size of mutant strains and the ‘sizer-timer-adder’ behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of size control in yeast and the role that the cell cycle plays in maintaining cell size.
the question of how cells measure their own size and use this measurement to regulate their growth and division.
the question of how cell size is measured and used to regulate the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cell cycle in budding yeast is controlled by a combination of inhibitor dilution in G1 and SBF titration in S/G2.
size control in S. cerevisiae is achieved by a combination of both dilution and titrational mechanisms, which are integrated into the cell cycle through positive and negative feedback loops.
size control in budding yeast is achieved by a combination of both inhibitor dilution and nuclear site titration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
size control is achieved through a combination of dilution and titrating of cell-cycle regulators, which is in line with the recent experimental findings.
the size of budding yeast cells is controlled by a combination of titration and dilution mechanisms.
cell size homeostasis in budding yeast is achieved by a positive feedback loop that couples cell growth to the cell cycle through the inhibitor dilution mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell cycle may be a key component of the size control machinery in budding yeast, and that size homeostasis may arise through the coupling of cell growth and the cell cycle.
cell-cycle regulators can be used to measure the size of a cell and control cell division.
size control can be achieved through different mechanisms that operate in different phases of the cell cycle.
